content.value_statement: Complex software projects need clear planning, testing, and review. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through SPARC phases with structured workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains the five SPARC phases from specification through completion.
Maps specialized modes to research, design, coding, testing, review, and documentation work.
Shows MCP and CLI activation patterns for Claude Flow based workflows.
Describes hierarchical, mesh, sequential, parallel, and adaptive orchestration patterns.
Provides workflow examples for feature development, bug investigation, optimization, and refactoring.
limitations: Does not install Claude Flow or verify local tool availability.
CLI examples require user approval and a trusted package source.
Does not replace project-specific architecture, security, or compliance review.
Benchmark claims in the skill file are not independently verified.

use_cases.title: Plan Feature Delivery
use_cases.description: Break a feature into specification, architecture, implementation, review, and completion phases with clear responsibilities.

use_cases.title: Run Test-Driven Work
use_cases.description: Create a red, green, refactor workflow that links tests, implementation, review, and documentation tasks.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Multi-Agent Reviews
use_cases.description: Select SPARC modes for research, code analysis, security review, performance tuning, and knowledge capture.

prompt_templates.title: Create a SPARC Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Use SPARC to plan this feature: [feature]. Include goals, constraints, phase order, roles, and completion criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Design a TDD Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a SPARC TDD workflow for [feature]. Include failing tests, implementation steps, review checks, and documentation tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate Parallel Modes
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a parallel SPARC workflow for [project]. Assign modes, dependencies, shared memory items, and checkpoints.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a Completed Feature
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate [feature] with SPARC completion standards. Cover architecture, tests, security, performance, documentation, and release readiness.

output_examples.input: Plan an authentication feature with SPARC.
output_examples.output: A five-phase delivery plan with requirements, architecture decisions, TDD tasks, review checks, and completion steps.

output_examples.input: Create a refactoring workflow for a legacy service.
output: Analysis tasks identify dependencies and risk areas.
Testing tasks build a safety net before changes.
Review tasks verify behavior, performance, and documentation.

output_examples.input: Coordinate research and implementation for a search feature.
output_examples.output: A mode sequence that links research, innovation, architecture, coding, testing, and documentation into one workflow.

best_practices: Define requirements and constraints before selecting modes.
Keep tests, review checks, and documentation tied to each phase.
Request explicit approval before running CLI commands from examples.
anti_patterns: Starting implementation before specification and architecture are clear.
Running broad parallel work without dependencies or checkpoints.
Treating generated plans as a substitute for project-specific review.

faq.question: What does SPARC mean?
faq.answer: SPARC means Specification, Pseudocode, Architecture, Refinement, and Completion.

faq.question: Does this skill write code automatically?
faq.answer: It provides methodology and workflow guidance. Actual code changes depend on the agent tools and user approval.

faq.question: Can I use it without Claude Flow?
faq.answer: Yes, you can use the phase structure manually. Claude Flow examples require the related tools or CLI.

faq.question: Is it only for new projects?
faq.answer: No. The skill also includes workflows for bug investigation, performance work, and legacy refactoring.

faq.question: Does it support test-driven development?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes red, green, refactor guidance and coverage-focused workflow examples.

faq.question: Should agents run the CLI examples automatically?
faq.answer: No. Agents should ask for user confirmation before running shell commands or installing packages.
